html:
The Suruwahá, or Zuruahã, are an Indigenous people of the Cuniuá area of the Purus River basin in Amazonas state, Brazil. They speak a language of the Arawan family, related to those of the Banawá, Jamamadi and Jarawara.

During the rubber boom they withdrew deep into the forest, and they had little contact with outsiders until the 1980s. They number only a few hundred. They are known to anthropologists for a high rate of suicide by drinking a fish poison, which has deep meaning in their beliefs about death.
